diagnostic_evidence.quote: for all $w\in \mathcal U$ one has $c(\cdot,w)\in L^{p^{\prime}}(\Omega)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof and estimator require the element residual R_T=s_h-div sigma_h to be a function in L^2(T): the oscillation term uses ||R_T||_{L^2(T)} and the Cauchy-Schwarz/Poincare step is in L^2. But the standing data assumption is only f in H^{-1}, and the coefficient assumptions only give c or B in L^{p'} (which can be below L^2 when p>2). H^{-1} data need not be locally integrable, so subtracting f elementwise, applying the L^1-based P0 projection, and forming an L^2 oscillation norm are not justified as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a standing certification hypothesis that the source term s_h is elementwise L^2 (for example f in L^2 and the reaction/lower-order contributions in L^2 on the relevant states), or else represent general H^{-1} data by an equilibrated flux and modify the residual splitting and oscillation term accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The guaranteed residual majorant for ingredient (C1), and the divergence-target flux construction that feeds it, are not well-defined or finite for the stated data class; the NK input r is certified only after extra source regularity is imposed.
issues.title: Residual majorant uses element L2 residuals without integrable/L2 source data
issues.why_classification: The L^2-source repair is contained and preserves the method for standard data, but it narrows the formally stated f in H^{-1} scope; retaining all H^{-1} data would require a different data-flux representation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$ be a bounded polyhedral Lipschitz domain.
we use the Sobolev embedding $V\hookrightarrow L^p(\Omega)$ with $p\in[2,\infty)$ if $d=2$ and $p\in[2,6]$ if $d=3$.
Therefore, the $u$-dependent diffusion model \eqref{eq:quasi-u-diffusion} satisfies (C3) on $B_{\rho}$.

issues.failure_explanation: In dimensions d=2 and d=3, H_0^1(Omega) does not embed into L^infinity(Omega); standard logarithmic singularities already give unbounded H^1 functions in 2D. Hence no computable constant C_infinity with the stated inequality for all v in V can exist, and no finite M_infinity(rho) can bound the L^infinity norm of every function in an energy ball B_rho. The later coefficient-difference estimates and the final L(rho) formula all depend on this impossible input.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Within the source-supported framework, remove or replace this example and exclude u-dependence of the principal diffusion coefficient from the certified C3 class in d=2,3 (or restrict to d=1). An L^infinity-based repair would require a stronger state space or extra regularity not supplied by the source.
issues.overall_effect: The representative proof that a principal diffusion coefficient depending on u satisfies the Lipschitz ingredient (C3) in the H^1 energy norm is invalid in the paper's dimensions; only semilinear or otherwise specially structured quasilinear examples remain supported.
issues.title: Quasilinear u-dependent diffusion example assumes a false H^1-to-L infinity embedding
issues.why_classification: No comparable H^1 energy-norm version of this primary claim survives in d=2,3; the supported fixes delete the advertised state-dependent principal-diffusion regime or add unsupported regularity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \langle \mathcal G(z_h),v\rangle := j_{\tilde u_h}(v)-B_{\tilde u_h}(v,z_h) \quad \forall v\in V.

issues.failure_explanation: The functional G(z_h)=j-B(.,z_h) is the negative of the standard primal residual B(z_h,.)-j. To reuse the equilibrated-flux majorant with mismatch sigma_h^*-A grad z_h, the source must be s_F=partial_s c(.,u_h) z_h - psi (equivalently the divergence target must have the opposite sign). With the stated s_h^*=psi-partial_s c z_h and div sigma_h^*=Pi_T^0(s_h^*), the bound need not control G. Counterexample: A=I, partial_s c=0, psi constant c, and z_h solving Delta z_h=c with zero boundary. Then sigma_h^*=grad z_h has div sigma_h^*=c=r_h^*, zero mismatch and zero stated element residual, but integration by parts gives G(z_h)(v)=2c integral_Omega v, a nonzero H^{-1} functional.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the equilibrated majorant to B(z_h,.)-j (whose norm equals ||G(z_h)||), i.e. flip the sign of the adjoint source/divergence target to s_F=partial_s c(.,u_h)z_h-psi before reconstruction.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guaranteed upper bound for the adjoint residual norm can underestimate ||G(z_h)||_{V*}, so adjoint-enhanced output enclosures produced through this remark are not rigorous until the sign is corrected; the abstract adjoint theorem remains valid only if a true upper bound for ||G(z_h)|| is supplied.
issues.title: Adjoint residual equilibration uses the opposite source sign
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local sign change in the adjoint source and divergence target; after it, the same Marini route and all output-enclosure claims survive with no new lemma or lost regime.

issues.failure_explanation: For eta>0 and L(rho)>0, p(rho)<=0 forces eta + positive term <= rho, hence every admissible radius is strictly larger than eta. If the initial test at rho=2 eta fails, the bracketing loop first tests rho_low=eta and then only rho<=eta; all these candidates have p(rho)=eta-rho+nonnegative term >0 and cannot be admissible. Thus the fallback necessarily returns fail and never searches the interval (eta,2 eta), or more generally (eta,rho_q), where admissible radii must lie when the quick test fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the shrinking fallback by a search constrained to rho>eta: use the monotone q-condition to bound the search above and locate the cubic p-sublevel interval (or sample/double upward from eta until an admissible point or a certified lower threshold is bracketed) before bisecting the upper endpoint.
issues.overall_effect: The certified radius-selection procedure has no effective fallback: whenever the quick test fails it can report failure even though the admissible set is nonempty. The NK existence theorem and the reported numerical radii obtained by the passing quick test are unaffected.
issues.title: Radius-selection fallback searches only radii that cannot be admissible
issues.why_classification: The fix requires changing the search logic, but it uses the existing scalar interval structure and does not weaken the NK theorem, the constants, or the reported non-fallback results.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof allows the strictly convex p-sublevel set to collapse to a point (rho_-=rho_+). At such a tangency the strict inequality q(rho)<1 can still hold, so the admissible set is a singleton {rho_*}, not a half-open interval [rho_-,rho_+). The later assertion that admissibility holds exactly below rho_+ then fails at the endpoint rho=rho_+.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the admissible set may also be a singleton, or impose a nondegenerate certified margin (for example require a strict p<0 point) before bisection, and adjust the endpoint inequalities to allow equality at an isolated admissible radius.
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's interval-structure justification and the endpoint inequalities used for the bisection correctness are not valid in the boundary case where the scalar NK conditions are tangent to admissibility; nondegenerate admissible intervals are unaffected.
issues.title: Admissible-radius lemma omits the degenerate singleton case
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate endpoint/case repair; all nondegenerate interval and bisection claims, and the main NK theorem, survive without changing the method or guarantees.
